src.text: Turkish coffee (boiled, unfiltered, about 7 g coffee per 70 ml cup) has no USDA record. Its caffeine was measured at 2.0–2.2 mg per ml (Derossi et al. 2018, J Sci Food Agric; one cup 112 mg) and 2.8 mg per ml (Elsahoryi et al. 2025). The USDA espresso record has the same strength (2.1 mg per g), so we use it for a 70 ml cup: about 148 mg caffeine. Your cup depends on how much coffee goes in and whether you drink the grounds. Range: caffeineMg 112–196 per serving.
src.cite: USDA FoodData Central, SR Legacy 171891: Beverages, coffee, brewed, espresso, restaurant-prepared

overrides.text: Burek: there is no USDA burek, so the values are from a Croatian producer’s cheese burek (Čakovečki mlinovi: 297 kcal, 16 g fat, 3.3 g sugar per 100 g). The web table does not print “per 100 g”, but EU law requires nutrition per 100 g, and the same table format gives a 400 g loaf 222 kcal, which can only be per 100 g. Burek varies: labels range from about 250 to 320 kcal per 100 g.
overrides.source: Čakovečki mlinovi, Burek (net weight 150 g; “slojevi tijesta i sirnog nadjeva”, layers of dough and cheese filling): energy 1241 kJ / 297 kcal, fat 16 g, saturates 7.5 g, carbohydrate 29 g, sugars 3.3 g, protein 9.7 g, salt 1.4 g. Basis: Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 Art. 32(2) “shall be expressed per 100 g or per 100 ml”. Range: Sofka beef burek 247 kcal, Lidl meat burek 316 kcal (Open Food Facts 9120018535583, 4056489610953)
overrides.note: Sodium = 1.4 / 2.5 = 560 mg. Fiber not declared (None). Water stays from the USDA turnover proxy. Basis checked 2026-10-19 on the producer's web page (EN and HR), not on the pack: the table has no column header; per 100 g follows from EU 1169/2011 Art. 32(2), from Atwater (16×9 + 29×4 + 9.7×4 = 299 kcal ≈ 297, i.e. 54.7 g of macros per 100 g, plausible for burek), from the same page's 400 g breads at 222 and 260 kcal (per 100 g), and from other burek labels (247-316 kcal/100 g); per piece it would be 198 kcal/100 g, below every label. Level B until read on the pack.

opts.name: pita

src.text: Pita: 100 g of bread (USDA white pita). Twenty döner kebabs bought and weighed in Italy (the same study as the meat) were 22–27% bread, about 100 g of a 402 g kebab; USDA’s gyro uses a 60 g pita. Blood sugar: white pita bread as tested in healthy people (Atkinson 2008 table A1, 68 ± 5), GI 68.
src.cite: Panozzo et al. 2015, Ital J Food Saf 4:4535 (20 weighed döner kebabs); RTL test via Mallorca Revue; USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro

opts.giSource: Atkinson 2008 (PMC2584181) Suppl. Table A1 (healthy subjects) row 295: Pita bread, white, mini (UK), 68 ± 5, 10 subjects; listed again in Atkinson 2021 Suppl. Table 1 row 347 (ISO method)

opts.name: wrap

src.text: Wrap: a 10-inch flour tortilla, 72 g (USDA; 49–117 g from 8 to 12 inches). Blood sugar: the only wheat-flour tortilla tested in healthy people (Mexico, 8 people, one test; Atkinson 2008 table A1), so it is uncertain, GI 30.
src.cite: USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro sandwich; weighed döner meat (RTL test, Mallorca Revue)

opts.giSource: Atkinson 2008 (PMC2584181) Suppl. Table A1 (healthy subjects) row 1845: Wheat tortilla (Mexico), 30 on the glucose scale (43 ± 7 on the bread scale), 8 subjects, single test; the 2021 edition lists it in Suppl. Table 2 because of the small number; no white flour wrap was tested

src.text: Chicken: 150 g of meat (roasted chicken thigh with skin, USDA). Twenty döner kebabs bought and weighed in Italy averaged 402 g with 35–40% meat, about 150 g; a German TV test weighed 80–173 g of meat; USDA’s gyro uses 60 g. The study found skin in the döner meat and 8.6 g of fat per 100 g of kebab, which skinless thigh meat cannot reach, so we use thigh with skin.
src.cite: Panozzo et al. 2015, Ital J Food Saf 4:4535 (20 weighed döner kebabs); RTL test via Mallorca Revue; USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro

src.text: Beef/veal: 150 g of meat; the closest USDA record is grilled ground beef 80/20 (German rules allow up to 60% minced meat in a döner). Weighed döner kebabs in Italy carried about 150 g of meat (35–40% of a 402 g kebab); measured portions run from 60 g (USDA gyro) to about 230 g.
src.cite: Panozzo et al. 2015, Ital J Food Saf 4:4535 (20 weighed döner kebabs); RTL test via Mallorca Revue; USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro

src.text: Tomato: 40 g. The weighed Italian kebabs carried about 100 g of vegetables in all (25% of 402 g); we split that into tomato 40 g, onion 25 g and lettuce 30 g (USDA’s gyro uses 30 g of tomato).
src.cite: Panozzo et al. 2015, Ital J Food Saf 4:4535 (20 weighed döner kebabs); RTL test via Mallorca Revue; USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro

src.text: Onion: 25 g, part of the about 100 g of vegetables in the weighed Italian kebabs (USDA’s gyro uses 20 g).
src.cite: Panozzo et al. 2015, Ital J Food Saf 4:4535 (20 weighed döner kebabs); RTL test via Mallorca Revue; USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro

src.text: Lettuce: 30 g, standing in for the salad and cabbage in the weighed Italian kebabs (about 100 g of vegetables in all).
src.cite: Panozzo et al. 2015, Ital J Food Saf 4:4535 (20 weighed döner kebabs); RTL test via Mallorca Revue; USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro

opts.name: yogurt sauce

src.text: Yogurt sauce: 38 g; plain whole-milk yogurt stands in. The weighed Italian kebabs carried about 52 g of sauce (13% of 402 g), often yogurt-based; with the 14 g of mayonnaise that makes 52 g (USDA’s gyro uses 30 g of tzatziki).
src.cite: Panozzo et al. 2015, Ital J Food Saf 4:4535 (20 weighed döner kebabs); RTL test via Mallorca Revue; USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro

opts.giSource: Atkinson 2021 (AJCN 114:1625) Suppl. Table 1 row 1046: No Added Sugar Natural yoghurt (Tamar Valley Dairy, Australia), 17 ± 2, 10 subjects (fat level not stated); Atkinson 2008 A1 row 892, fat-free natural yoghurt, 19 ± 5

src.text: Mayonnaise sauce: 14 g (USDA guideline amount on a regular sandwich). The Italian study reports that kebab shops mostly used supermarket mayonnaise and ketchup; without it the kebab has about a third less fat than the study measured.
src.cite: Panozzo et al. 2015, Ital J Food Saf 4:4535 (20 weighed döner kebabs); RTL test via Mallorca Revue; USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro

src.text: Kebab is our builder: pita or wrap, chicken or beef, vegetables and sauce, each a USDA record. The amounts follow twenty döner kebabs bought and weighed in Italian shops (402 g: 37% meat, 25% bread, 25% vegetables, 13% sauce). Our default has about the study’s measured fat and protein per 100 g. The study’s 226 kcal per 100 g is gross energy from burning the food in a calorimeter; the energy the body can use from its measured protein, fat and starch is about 177–187 kcal per 100 g, and ours is 192. Kebab shops differ a lot, mostly in the meat.
src.cite: Panozzo et al. 2015, Ital J Food Saf 4:4535 (20 weighed döner kebabs); RTL test via Mallorca Revue; USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro

src.text: Poke bowl: the RecipeTin Eats tuna poke bowl for 4, one bowl: 87.5 g raw tuna (USDA yellowfin), 1/2 cup sushi rice (100 g raw, as cooked USDA rice by its carbohydrate) seasoned with 1 tbsp rice vinegar and 1/2 tsp sugar, about 2 tsp soy sauce and 2 1/2 tsp sesame oil, 1/4 small avocado (34 g: a quarter of USDA's 136 g Hass avocado, values of USDA's all-varieties record), 1/4 cup edamame, 1/4 cucumber, 1/4 carrot, 1 1/2 radishes and 1/4 green onion (USDA portions). The 2 tbsp of mirin in the dressing (for 4) have no USDA record and are not counted. RecipeTin Eats' own estimate is 591 kcal a bowl; ours, from the USDA parts, is higher, mostly the rice.

src.text: Spaghetti carbonara: the Giallo Zafferano recipe for 4 (320 g spaghetti, 150 g guanciale, 6 egg yolks, 50 g Pecorino Romano, black pepper), one plate: 80 g dry spaghetti (also the Italian standard portion, ISS / CREA) as 194 g cooked (USDA pasta, by its carbohydrate), 37.5 g cured pork (USDA raw bacon: USDA has no guanciale, a fattier cut), 1.5 yolks (USDA large yolk, 17 g each) and 12.5 g pecorino (USDA Romano). The rendered fat stays in the sauce; the salt in the pasta water is not counted.
